title: rmrodell/nanomodamp pipeline parameters
description: Nano-BID-Amp pseudouridine site calling from demultiplexed Nanopore amplicon FASTQ

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the sample sheet (CSV) describing the samples of one run. Use either --input or --input_counts.
input.help_text: Comma-separated sample sheet with a header row. Required columns: `sample_id`, `fastq` (a `.fastq.gz` file or a directory whose `*.fastq.gz` files are concatenated in lexical order), `treat` (`input` or `BS`) and `rep` (batch-paired replicate). Any other column is carried as metadata. Relative `fastq` paths are resolved against the sample sheet's directory. See docs/usage.md and docs/contracts/samplesheet.md.

input_counts.description: Comma-separated `counts_merged.tsv` files from earlier runs, or a directory of them. Skips preprocessing and counting; the tables are merged and site calling runs on the result. Use either --input or --input_counts.
input_counts.help_text: D32. For runs that need different preprocessing parameters (for example a legacy library and a standard one): run each with --input and no --analyses, then merge their counts/counts_merged.tsv with --input_counts and --analyses. Tables are merged by column name (R-06); metadata columns are the union (missing values become NA, with a warning). Duplicate sample_id across tables or differing count/site columns stop the run. Output: counts/counts_merged.tsv and counts/merge_sources.tsv.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_options.title: Library and reference options
reference_options.description: Library type, reference sequences and target regions. Required with --input (not used with --input_counts).

library_type.help_text: `endogenous` (transcript amplicons) or `mpra` (oligo pool). Sets the minimap2 default (D5) and enables the MPRA pool-adapter trim. One library type per run.

fasta.description: Reference FASTA: transcript sequences (endogenous) or the oligo pool (MPRA).
fasta.help_text: The `.fai` index is always rebuilt on a copy of the FASTA (decompressed if `.gz`); a `.fai` supplied next to the FASTA is ignored (R-31).

bed.description: BED file of amplicons or single sites (≥ 6 columns).
bed.help_text: Whole amplicons or single sites (D11). Strand should be `+` (D19); other strands give a warning.

bed_coordinates.description: BED coordinate convention: `bed0` (standard, default) or `one_based_start` (legacy paper BEDs).
bed_coordinates.help_text: D27, R-15 (decided at G1-e). `bed0`: standard 0-based, half-open BED (a single site at 1-based position p is `start = p-1, end = p`). `one_based_start`: the legacy reading used for the paper's BEDs, where start and end are both 1-based and inclusive (a single site is `start = end = p`). Under `bed0`, any row with start = end is an error that points to `one_based_start`; the convention is never auto-detected.

adapter_options.title: Orientation and adapter trimming
adapter_options.description: Adapter sequences and cutadapt settings (plan §6.1; D4, D29, D31).

orientation_adapters.description: Adapters used to orient reads. Keep the default `ont` for all libraries built with ONT adapters, including MPRA in cellulo.
orientation_adapters.help_text: D29. `ont` (default, for all endogenous, MPRA in vitro and MPRA in cellulo data): sense/antisense passes use the ONT adapters, followed by the MPRA pool trim for `library_type=mpra`. `pool` is an opt-in exception for legacy libraries built without ONT adapters (the paper's in-cellulo run 20241114, used by `test_golden`): the passes use the MPRA pool adapters with the `trim1_*` settings and the separate pool trim is skipped. `pool` requires `library_type=mpra` and `umi=false`. Never set from `library_type`.

ont_adapter_mode.description: How the ONT adapters are trimmed. Keep the default `linked` for all libraries built with both ONT adapters.
ont_adapter_mode.help_text: D31. `linked` (default, all data): sense and antisense passes each require both ONT adapters (D4). `three_prime_only` is an opt-in exception for legacy libraries whose reads lack the 5′ ONT adapter (the paper's endogenous run 20250418, used by `test_golden`): a single `cutadapt -m {trim1_min_length} -O {trim1_min_overlap} -a <ont_adapter_sense_3p>` pass that keeps untrimmed reads, with no antisense pass or reverse complement; the read funnel records `trim1_3prime`. Valid only with `orientation_adapters=ont`. Never set from `library_type`.

ont_adapter_antisense_5p.description: ONT antisense 5′ adapter; must be the reverse complement of the sense 3′ adapter (checked at startup).

ont_adapter_antisense_3p.description: ONT antisense 3′ adapter; must be the reverse complement of the sense 5′ adapter (checked at startup).

pool_adapter_antisense_5p.description: Pool antisense 5′ adapter, used only with `orientation_adapters=pool`; reverse complement of `pool_adapter_3p` (checked at startup).

pool_adapter_antisense_3p.description: Pool antisense 3′ adapter, used only with `orientation_adapters=pool`; reverse complement of `pool_adapter_5p` (checked at startup).

trim2_min_length.description: cutadapt `-m` for the MPRA pool trim (MPRA only).

trim2_min_overlap.description: cutadapt `-O` for the MPRA pool trim (MPRA only).

require_both_adapters.description: Keep only reads with both linked adapters (D4).
require_both_adapters.help_text: `false` reproduces the legacy non-anchored behaviour (R-04) and is for diagnostics only.

umi_options.title: UMI and deduplication
umi_options.description: UMI extraction and UMICollapse deduplication (D7, D29).

umi.description: Extract UMIs and deduplicate. Keep the default `true` for all libraries with UMIs, including MPRA in cellulo.
umi.help_text: D29. `false` is an opt-in exception for legacy libraries built without UMIs (the paper's in-cellulo run 20241114, used by `test_golden`): UMI extraction and UMICollapse are skipped and the filtered BAM is the final BAM; the read funnel omits `umi_extracted` and `dedup`. Never set from `library_type`.

minimap2_args.description: minimap2 arguments. Empty = by library type: `mpra` → `-ax sr`, `endogenous` → `-ax splice -uf`.
minimap2_args.help_text: D5: these are the presets validated in the paper; presets change how deletions are represented. See docs/methods.md before changing them.

min_mapq.description: Keep alignments with MAPQ ≥ this value (`samtools view -q`).

counting_options.title: Counting
counting_options.description: Per-site pileup counting (plan §6.2; D9, D10, D12).

min_coverage.description: Keep sites with `totalReads > min_coverage` (strict; D10, R-13).

pileup_max_depth.description: Rsamtools pileup `max_depth`; a warning is issued when reached (R-16).

count_all_bases.description: QC mode: report all reference bases and the background-deletion report (D12). Site calling still uses T only.

kmer_size.description: Centered k-mer length reported per site; NA near sequence ends.

allow_region_failures.description: If false, any per-region counting error fails the task (R-12). Failed regions are always written to `failed_regions.tsv`.

analyses.description: YAML file of analyses and site sets. If absent, the pipeline stops after counting.
analyses.help_text: Format: assets/schema_analyses.json and docs/contracts/analyses.md. Checked at startup (names, types, factor levels, site-set references); full validation is part of site calling.

plot_all_sites.description: Write the all-sites plot for every analysis (per-analysis override allowed).

golden_experiment.description: Golden experiment to run with `-profile test_golden`.
golden_experiment.help_text: One golden run per paper sequencing run. The only places the pipeline sets non-default preprocessing modes: `endogenous_20250418` uses `ont_adapter_mode=three_prime_only` (D31) and `mpra_incell` (run 20241114) uses `orientation_adapters=pool, umi=false` (D29), because those libraries were built without the 5′ ONT adapter or without ONT adapters and UMIs. Endogenous takes three runs (D32): `endogenous_20250418` and `endogenous_20251022` preprocess and count, then `endogenous` merges their counts with `--input_counts` and calls sites (see conf/test_golden.config).

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
